accepted.s: Under which scheme is the Andhra Pradesh Micro Irrigation Project implemented throughout the State with financial assistance?

accepted.s: Variable-rate technology in agriculture refers to the practice of:
o: changing the crop variety every season without field data
applying the same quantity of inputs throughout a field
using only variable rainfall for crop production
applying inputs at varying rates within a field according to sensor or GIS maps
accepted.x: Variable-rate technology applies agricultural inputs at different rates within a field, based on sensor information or GIS maps.
accepted.tq: Distinguish precision-based variation from uniform field application.
accepted.sec: Precision agriculture tools - GPS, GIS, remote sensing, variable-rate technology, soil sensors

accepted.s: GPS, drones, artificial intelligence and sensors are identified as core elements of which agricultural approach?

accepted.tq: Identify the exact conceptual grouping of related technologies.

accepted.s: Which of the following is identified as a criticism or continuing concern regarding resource-efficient irrigation and agriculture?
o: Drip irrigation has no initial cost and irrigation has shifted entirely away from rice
Drip irrigation has a high upfront cost and irrigation remains skewed towards rice
Solar pumps are prohibited in State irrigation plans
Precision agriculture cannot use sensors or data analytics
accepted.x: The stated concerns are the high upfront cost of drip irrigation and the continuing skew of irrigation towards rice.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing both recognised limitations without reversing the comparison.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which combination correctly represents the way forward identified for Andhra Pradesh in the APSES 2024-25?

Only flood irrigation and manual crop assessment
Precision farming, drones, IoT, drip and sprinkler irrigation, and rainwater harvesting
accepted.x: APSES 2024-25 identifies precision farming, drones, IoT, drip and sprinkler irrigation, and rainwater harvesting as the way forward.
